subject: Intermittent egress failures from ClearWave on hybrid deployment
messages:
From: ops@clearwave.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ClearWave] spikes of 502/connection resets after on-prem cutover

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

We cut over the ClearWave on-prem appliance to the Redwood Private tunnel at 03:00 local and are seeing intermittent 502s and TCP resets for our API traffic to the hosted inference endpoint. Memory/CPU on our appliance looks normal. Traceroute from our egress shows path divergence to two different transit routers depending on flow. Attach: clearwave-tcpdump.pcap and a short traceroute log.

What we see: many client→Redwood sessions succeed, but ~5-10% fail with RST or 504s after ~3s. TCP dump shows retransmits and MSS-clamped packets. We suspect some translation or MTU/clamping mismatch at your side or on the hybrid VPN.

Can you advise next steps? We can open a maintenance window tonight if you need changes on Redwoods VPC side.

Thanks,
Jin Park
Network Ops, ClearWave Solutions
ops@clearwave.com

Attachments: clearwave-tcpdump.pcap (packet capture), traceroute-logs.txt (text)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: ops@clearwave.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] spikes of 502/connection resets after on-prem cutover

Thanks Jin — sorry youre hitting this right after cutover. Ive started a quick triage:

- Can you confirm whether you applied MSS clamping on the VPN/jumbo-paths? The pcap looks like MTU reduction + extra headers, which causes fragmentation and retransmits.
- Do you see any conntrack counters spike on the appliance (SYN_RECV/SYN_RETRY)? If ephemeral ports are being NATed without sufficient range we can run out and see resets.
- Well check our VPC NAT gateway and the Dedicated tunnel config; jonas, can you start with conntrack snapshot and iptables rules from the hybrid egress nodes?

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
1) If you can enable MSS clamp to 1360 on the ClearWave tunnel on a short window, that often resolves fragmentation-related resets.
2) We can pin a small pool of SNAT addresses for your VPN prefix to reduce asymmetry while we investigate.

Im CCing Jonas for infra-level checks and will follow up once he posts findings. If this is high-impact for you we can do a 1h maintenance tonight 23:00-00:00 PDT.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Private Deployments (interim)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearwave.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] spikes of 502/connection resets after on-prem cutover

Triage notes (quick dump from hybrid-egress-03):

- Conntrack snapshot (attached) shows large number of TIME_WAIT + REUSE entries tied to the ClearWave prefix 198.51.100.0/24; ephemeral port churn is high.
- iptables SNAT rule currently does: -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j SNAT --to-source 34.210.149.102 (single address). That single SNAT is causing port exhaustion under concurrent flows.
- I tested a quick change locally: switch SNAT to a small range (34.210.149.102-34.210.149.110) and tuned net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max up by 20% — in the lab this eliminated RSTs under identical load.

Commands I recommend for a maintenance window:
1) iptables -t nat -R POSTROUTING -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j SNAT --to-source 34.210.149.102-34.210.149.110
2) sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288 (persist via /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf)
3) confirm conntrack-timeouts for ESTABLISHED are reasonable (tcp_fin_timeout / tcp_keepalive)
4) If you have a hardware VPN path, apply MSS clamp to 1360 on the ClearWave tunnel at their edge.

Im attaching the conntrack snapshot: conntrack-snapshot.txt.

If we schedule the maintenance tonight I can push these iptables changes and monitor for 30m. Marissa — can you confirm whether we have permission to allocate that SNAT block for ClearWave?

-Jonas
Infra Eng, Private Deployment Runtime

Attachments: conntrack-snapshot.txt

From: ops@clearwave.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-23T07:49:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] spikes of 502/connection resets after on-prem cutover

Thanks Jonas — we applied MSS clamp to 1360 on the on-prem appliance and reduced MTU on the VPN. After that we still observed a subset of flows failing; traceroute indicates some flows are hairpinned through an older transit hop (asymmetric route). Sample traceroute block:

1  10.0.0.1  1.123 ms
2  198.51.100.5  2.234 ms
3  203.0.113.22  12.512 ms
4  * * *
5  34.210.149.102  48.129 ms

Were concerned about source address preservation: when Redwoods egress SNATs traffic, is the original source preserved behind a pinned SNAT? If SNAT mapping moves between egress nodes mid-flow that could create asymmetry.

Were willing to run your suggested small SNAT pool in the maintenance window — please confirm the exact addresses and expected timeline. Also, is there a way to avoid SNAT entirely for this peer (i.e., preserve ClearWave source IP) so we can do end-to-end provenance for logs?

Jin

Attachments: traceroute-post-mss.txt

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ops@clearwave.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-24T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] spikes of 502/connection resets after on-prem cutover - remediation plan

Summary and plan:

1) Root cause: single-address SNAT + high ephemeral port churn + asymmetric routing after cutover. Combination caused apparent connection resets when mappings were exhausted or shifted between egress nodes. MSS/MTU contributed to retransmits but was not the primary cause.

2) Short-term mitigation (tonight 23:00-00:00 PDT maintenance window):
   - Allocate SNAT pool 34.210.149.102-34.210.149.110 for ClearWave (reservation approved by infra).
   - Increase conntrack limit to 524288 on hybrid-egress nodes and apply tuned tcp_fin_timeout=30.
   - Monitor for 60 minutes post-change; collect conntrack and tcpdump samples.

3) Medium-term:
   - We will evaluate peerwise source-preservation for your prefix; full preserve requires route exchange and static mapping on the hybrid gateway (requires a formal peer config change and possibly a BGP session). Ive opened Jira SUP-8452 to track the engineering work.

4) Postmortem notes: well produce a short runbook covering SNAT allocation, conntrack tuning, and MSS recommendations for on-prem partners. Draft attached: runbook-egress-fix.md.

Please confirm youre ok with tonights window and well proceed. If you prefer we can do an earlier window — let me know.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-egress-fix.md
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-8452
